headline: India Achieves Landmark 300 GW Non-Fossil Fuel Power Capacity
fullText:
Ministry of New and Renewable Energy

India Achieves Landmark 300 GW Non-Fossil Fuel Power Capacity

09 AUG 2026 2:31PM by PIB Delhi

In a major milestone for the nation's clean energy transition and climate action targets, India has crossed 300 GW of non-fossil fuel-based installed electricity generation capacity as on 31st July, 2026; over 60% of the 500 GW capacity targeted to be achieved by 2030.

Breakdown of Non-Fossil Fuel Capacity (as on 31.07.2026):

Solar Power: 164.59 GW

Wind Power: 58.14 GW

Hydro Power (Large & Small): 57.24 GW

Bio-power: 11.75 GW

Nuclear Power: 8.78 GW

Total Non-Fossil Capacity: 300.50 GW

The share of non-fossil fuel electricity capacity in the country’s total electricity generation capacity (which is around 552 GW at present), has reached over 54%.

Backed through the key policy enablers provided by the Government for this transformation, this monumental achievement highlights India’s rapid progress towards building an Aatmanirbhar energy ecosystem and securing the target of 500 GW non-fossil capacity by 2030.

The growth in clean energy generation has been anchored by stellar contributions across sectors. Solar energy remains the key growth engine with around 165 GW at present from just 2.8 GW in 2014. Concurrently, the wind energy sector has also seen strong momentum reaching to over 58 GW from 21 GW in 2014.

During 2025-26, a record capacity of 55.29 GW non-fossil fuel based electricity capacity was installed in the country with key contributions from 44.6 GW solar power and 6 GW wind power.

The rapid progress in renewable energy capacity is also reflected in renewable energy generation in the country which has increased from 190.96 billion units in 2014-15 to 477.79 BU in 2025-26.

To support this rapid expansion and ensure supply chain independence, India has transformed its domestic manufacturing capabilities. Driven by the Production Linked Incentive (PLI) scheme focusing on the nation's solar installations with high-efficiency, indigenously produced modules, the enlisted capacity under the Approved List of Models and Manufacturers (ALMM) for Solar PV Modules has crossed the historic 200 GW milestone, rising from just 2.3 GW in 2014.

Clean energy transition is no longer just a climate commitment—it is central to shaping India's industrial competitiveness, energy independence, and economic resilience.

The Ministry of New and Renewable Energy is also driving deep industrial decarbonization, positioning India to become a global hub for the production, usage, and export of Green Hydrogen and its derivatives, through the implementation of the National Green Hydrogen Mission.

He urged the people, particularly the youth, to make blood donation a culture. “When we celebrate 100 years of our independence in 2047, our aim should not be limited to a developed economy; we must also envision a compassionate society where people are healthy and safe, and precious resources like blood are readily available in times of need,” he said.

Calling upon the youth to prioritise fitness, Raksha Mantri emphasised that a healthy and fit individual becomes a greater asset to society and is better equipped to undertake noble causes such as blood donation. Highlighting Maharashtra’s enduring tradition of valour and compassion, Shri Rajnath Singh said that the legacy of Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj continues to inspire generations. He emphasised that the true purpose of physical strength lies in protecting others and safeguarding the nation, adding that the contribution of the athletes and wrestlers from the land of Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj would be remembered as a noble service to the nation.

The event was attended by Deputy Chief Minister of Maharashtra Shri Eknath Shinde; Minister of State for Ayush (Independent Charge) Shri Pratap Rao Jadhav; Minister of Industries, Government of Maharashtra Shri Uday Ravindra Samant; Member of Parliament Dr Srikant Lata Eknath Shinde; Chief of the Army Staff General Dhiraj Seth; DG Armed Forces Medical Services (AFMS) Surgeon Vice Admiral Arti Sarin; Adjutant General Lt Gen VPS Kaushik; Commandant, Base Hospital, Delhi Cantt Maj Gen Vishal Chaudhary and other senior military & civil dignitaries.

headline: Government Strengthens Monitoring of Funds Earmarked for Welfare and Development of Scheduled Castes under DAPSC
fullText:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment

Government Strengthens Monitoring of Funds Earmarked for Welfare and Development of Scheduled Castes under DAPSC

38 Ministries/Departments Earmarking Funds under Development Action Plan for Scheduled Castes; Periodic Reviews Undertaken to Ensure Optimal Utilisation

09 AUG 2026 12:53PM by PIB Delhi

The Government has informed the Rajya Sabha that, as per the NITI Aayog Guidelines, 2017 for the Development Action Plan for Scheduled Castes (DAPSC), earlier known as the Scheduled Caste Sub-Plan (SCSP), 38 Ministries/Departments of the Government of India are earmarking funds across various schemes for the welfare and development of Scheduled Castes.

Minister of State for Social Justice and Empowerment Shri Ramdas Athawale shared these details in reply to Questions asked by SHRI GOLLA BABURAO in Rajya Sabha regarding the Development Action Plan for Scheduled Castes.

The data on Budget Estimates (BE), Revised Estimates (RE) and actual expenditure under DAPSC across Ministries/Departments since 2020-21 shows that actual expenditure remained below the Revised Estimates during each of the years from 2020-21 to 2025-26. The utilisation of Revised Estimates was 81.61 per cent in 2020-21, 91.22 per cent in 2021-22, 91.90 per cent in 2022-23, 93.83 per cent in 2023-24, 92.57 per cent in 2024-25 and 85.65 per cent in 2025-26.

The Government stated that the funds are earmarked only for the welfare of Scheduled Castes. However, due to the general nature of schemes in some Ministries/Departments, the funds are not utilised fully in certain cases.

The Department of Social Justice and Empowerment oversees the utilisation of DAPSC funds by the obligated Ministries/Departments through periodic review meetings under the chairpersonship of the Hon’ble Minister and Secretary, Social Justice and Empowerment. In the recent past, review meetings under DAPSC were held under the chairpersonship of Shri B.L. Verma, Hon’ble Minister of State for Social Justice and Empowerment, on April 29, 2025, and at the level of Secretary, Social Justice and Empowerment on August 25, 2025 and April 16, 2026.

From time to time, through communications, DAPSC-obligated Ministries/Departments are asked to expedite expenditure and ensure optimal utilisation of funds earmarked under DAPSC. Further, in adherence to the directions issued by the Minister of Social Justice and Empowerment, all 38 Ministries/Departments implementing DAPSC have nominated a nodal officer for financial and physical monitoring of DAPSC funds in their respective Ministries/Departments.

The Government continues to strengthen monitoring and review mechanisms to ensure optimal utilisation of funds earmarked under DAPSC for the welfare and development of Scheduled Castes.

headline: ₹1,178.20 Crore Central Share Released to Karnataka Under Post-Matric Scholarship for SC Students During Last Three Financial Years
fullText:

₹421.08 Crore Released in 2023-24, ₹422.90 Crore in 2024-25 and ₹334.22 Crore in 2025-26

09 AUG 2026 12:52PM by PIB Delhi

The Government has informed the Rajya Sabha that a total Central share of ₹1,178.20 crore was released to beneficiaries in Karnataka under the Centrally Sponsored Post-Matric Scholarship Scheme for Scheduled Caste (SC) students during the last three financial years.

Minister of State for Social Justice and Empowerment Shri Ramdas Athawale shared these details in reply to Unstarred Question No. 2050 in the Rajya Sabha regarding Central funds for Scheduled Caste welfare in Karnataka.

The Central share released under the Post-Matric Scholarship Scheme for SC students to beneficiaries in Karnataka was ₹421.08 crore in 2023-24, ₹422.90 crore in 2024-25 and ₹334.22 crore in 2025-26, amounting to a total of ₹1,178.20 crore during the three financial years.

The Department of Social Justice and Empowerment implements the Post-Matric Scholarship for Scheduled Castes (SCs) students as a Centrally Sponsored Scheme through State Governments and Union Territory Administrations. The scheme is being implemented through Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) mode with effect from 2021-22.

Under the scheme, release of the Central share of scholarship is contingent upon the State Governments and Union Territory Administrations sharing the finally verified State/UT-paid data on the National Scholarship Portal. The scheme is open-ended and demand-driven for all eligible students of recognized institutions across India.

With regard to the Development Action Plan for Scheduled Castes (DAPSC), the Government stated that NITI Aayog issued guidelines in 2017 for earmarking funds under DAPSC. As per these guidelines, each obligated Ministry/Department allocates funds under DAPSC for the socio-economic development of Scheduled Castes through its respective schemes.

These schemes are implemented by the concerned Ministries/Departments, while allocation of funds to States and Union Territories, including Karnataka, is undertaken by the respective Ministries/Departments in accordance with the guidelines of their schemes. The funds allocated by obligated Ministries/Departments under DAPSC are reflected in Statement 10A of the Expenditure Profile of the Union Budget.

The Government's response highlights the implementation of scholarship support for eligible Scheduled Caste students in Karnataka through a demand-driven mechanism and Direct Benefit Transfer-based delivery system.

Addressing the gathering at the State Function and Tiranga Concert on Vande Mataram at the DBRAIT Auditorium, the Vice-President said there could be no more appropriate place to launch the campaign than these historic islands, which are deeply associated with India’s freedom struggle and the history of the Tricolour.

Vice President Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan graced the State Function on ‘Har Ghar Tiranga - Dedicated to the Spirit of Vande Mataram’ at the DBRAIT Auditorium, in Sri Vijaya Puram, Andaman & Nicobar Islands today.

Recalling the immortal words of the great Tamil poet Subramania Bharati, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan said Bharati’s celebration of the ‘Mani Kodi’ reflects the eternal courage of the Indian spirit and the glory of the flag of Mother Bharat. He said the Har Ghar Tiranga Abhiyan carries forward this spirit by bringing every citizen together under one National Flag, one motherland and one common destiny.

Recalling the sacrifices of freedom fighters who endured the dreaded Kala Pani, the Vice President said the Andaman & Nicobar Islands are much more than a geographical part of Bharat; they are a sacred land of sacrifice. He paid heartfelt tributes to Veer Vinayak Damodar Savarkar and countless other patriots who suffered in the Cellular Jail, saying their courage, patriotism and sacrifice continue to inspire generations.

The Vice-President recalled that Mahatma Gandhi’s clarion call of “Do or Die” on August 8, 1942, awakened millions of Indians and gave a decisive impetus to the freedom struggle. He also highlighted the unique place of the islands in the history of the Tricolour, recalling that Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose hoisted the Indian National Flag here on December 30, 1943, marking a landmark moment in India’s freedom struggle.

Highlighting the significance of Har Ghar Tiranga, Shri Radhakrishnan said the campaign, initiated by Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, has evolved into a nationwide people’s movement. He called upon every citizen to proudly display the Tricolour and imbibe the values of patriotism, unity and collective responsibility that it represents. “Bharat is one and will always remain one,” he affirmed.

The Vice-President highlighted the islands as a living example of ‘Unity in Diversity’ and ‘Ek Bharat, Shreshtha Bharat’, while acknowledging their rich tribal heritage and recent progress in connectivity, healthcare, education and infrastructure. He said the Great Nicobar Island Development Project would further strengthen India’s maritime capabilities, connectivity and economic opportunities, while balancing development with environmental conservation.

Emphasising the need for national strength alongside India’s tradition of peace and generosity, Shri Radhakrishnan said, “India has always been generous, but our generosity should never be mistaken for weakness. We must remain prepared to protect our national interests and sovereignty.” He called upon citizens to let the Tricolour inspire them with courage, unity and hope, and to carry forward the legacy of the freedom fighters in building a stronger and developed Bharat.

The Vice-President also attended a cultural programme and visited the ‘Har Ghar Tiranga’ Exhibition, showcasing the spirit of the campaign and its message of national unity and patriotism.

The event was attended by Lieutenant Governor of Andaman & Nicobar Islands Admiral D. K. Joshi (Retd.), Chief Secretary Smt. Chanchal Yadav, Chairperson of Sri Vijaya Puram Municipal Council Smt. M. Vasantha and Adhyaksh, Zilla Parishad, Shri P. Ummer, among other dignitaries.
